title: Local invariant-monoid charts of the abelian-inertia modification
statement:
Let $f:(X,Z)\to(S,D)$ be a log smooth morphism of Noetherian quasi-excellent separated fs log regular pairs [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale], [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $X$ be integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and regular with $Z$ a strict normal crossings boundary, let a finite group $G$ act tamely over $S$ with trivial action on $S$, freely outside $Z$, with abelian geometric inertia groups and $G$-strict boundary. Strict normal crossings means regular components meeting regularly in the expected codimension; $G$-strict means distinct translates of a component are disjoint. Apply only the fourth-stage modification $b:X'\to X$ of [lem-per-gabber-absolute-equivariant-modification], giving $X'$ the inverse-image boundary $Z'=b^{-1}Z$.

Etale locally on the quotient and on $S$, and after replacing $G$ by a geometric inertia group, this construction is the strict base change of the following toric construction. Let $N$ be the exponent of this inertia group and $\mu_N$ the group of $N$th roots of unity. There are a localization $\Lambda$ of $\mathbf Z[1/N,\mu_N]$, a sharp fs monoid $Q$ charting $S$, $P=\mathbf Z^t\oplus\mathbf N^r$, and a map $\gamma:Q\to P$ with injective group completion whose cokernel has finite torsion subgroup of order invertible in $\Lambda$. Enlarge $P$ to $\overline P=P\oplus\mathbf N^s$ by adjoining eigenvector coordinates for the smooth directions. A character map $\chi:\overline P^{\rm gp}\to\operatorname{Hom}(G,\mu_N)$ defines
$$\overline R=\ker(\chi)\cap\overline P,\qquad R=\overline R\cap P.$$
The map $Q\to\overline P$ factors through $R$. The inclusion $\overline R^{\rm gp}\subset\overline P^{\rm gp}$ has finite index annihilated by an invertible integer. The regular saturated log blowup tower of $\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[\overline R]$ has affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[\overline R']$, where $\overline R'=\mathbf Z^a\oplus\mathbf N^b$ and $\nu^{\rm gp}:\overline R^{\rm gp}\to\overline R'^{\rm gp}$ is an isomorphism. Number the boundary coordinates so that the inverse image of the original boundary consists precisely of the first $c$ of the $b$ coordinate divisors, for $0\le c\le b$. Its log structure has chart
$$R'=\mathbf Z^a\oplus\mathbf N^c\subset\overline R',\qquad \nu(R)\subset R'.$$
Thus the quotient of $(X',Z')$ is locally a strict etale neighborhood of the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[\overline R']$ endowed with chart $R'$ along $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[Q]$. All group maps $Q^{\rm gp}\to R'^{\rm gp}\to\overline R'^{\rm gp}$ are the maps induced by this construction. The scheme map $\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[\overline R']\to\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[R']$ is affine space of dimension $b-c$. These local models and their quotients agree under strict inertia-preserving comparison maps and compute the globally glued fourth stage.

source.place: VIII 5.3.8, 5.4.4, 5.5.3--5.5.5, pp.125--129; X 1.8, pp.146--148, the diagrams (1.a)--(1.d), invariant monoids and retained boundary. This states the local construction, without asserting relative log smoothness.

proof.text: Use [lem-per-gabber-fixed-locus-log-chart] at the geometric point and replace $G$ by inertia. It gives $Q,P,\gamma,\Lambda$, fixed unit coordinates $u_j$, eigenparameters $z_i$, the finite free representation $V$, and the strict equivariant etale comparison with $S\times_\Sigma Y$. Keep this non-sharp chart; do not apply a sharp-chart theorem to $P$. To diagonalize $V$, localize the cyclotomic coefficient ring at the image prime and apply [lem-per-local-cyclotomic-group-algebra-split]. Because $G$ is abelian, its group algebra is commutative, so all matrix sizes in that statement are $1$. Its product idempotents decompose $V$ into finite projective summands on each of which every $g$ acts by a scalar $\psi(g)$. These scalars satisfy $\psi(g)^N=1$ and give characters into $\mu_N$: $T^N-1$ splits with distinct roots whose pairwise differences are units after inverting $N$, and the coefficient ring is local. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] these finitely many summands become free after localization near the chosen prime. Their bases give the required $y_i$, hence $\overline P=P\oplus\mathbf N^s$ and $\chi$. This explicitly allows the localization of $\Lambda$ needed for the eigenbasis. Since every prime divisor of $|G|$ divides the exponent $N$, $|G|$ is invertible in $\Lambda$.

source.place: X 1.2--1.3 and 1.8, pp.136--140,146; eigenline decomposition in the first paragraph of 1.8.

proof.text: The coefficient ring and the polynomial charts used below are regular. Indeed $A=\mathbf Z[1/N]$ is regular: its nonzero prime local rings have maximal ideal generated by that prime, and its zero-prime localization is a field. Put $\Phi=\Phi_N(T)$ and $T^N-1=\Phi(T)\Psi(T)$. At a primitive root $\zeta$ the identity $\Phi'(\zeta)\Psi(\zeta)=N\zeta^{N-1}$ shows that $\Phi'(\zeta)$ is a unit. Thus $A[\zeta]$ is the standard etale algebra for $\Phi$ in [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative]. Its one-equation Jacobian determinant is a unit, so [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra] makes it standard smooth and [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-is-smooth] makes it a smooth ring map, and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] gives regularity. Its localization $\Lambda$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring]. Applying [lem-trf-polynomial-ring-regular-base] and then localization gives regularity of $\Lambda[\mathbf Z^a][x_1,\ldots,x_b]$ for every $a,b$. A coordinate boundary is strict normal crossings: all its intersections are the regular rings obtained by deleting the corresponding variables. In particular the enlarged coordinate pair in the toric model is log regular by [lem-per-regular-boundary-divisorial-chart].

source.place: X 1.3 and 1.8, pp.139--140,146--148, the cyclotomic coefficient ring and regular coordinate models; explicit coefficient-ring check.

proof.text: Put $L=\ker\chi$ in $\overline P^{\rm gp}=\mathbf Z^{t+r+s}$ and $\overline R=L\cap\overline P$. Averaging on $\Lambda[\overline P]$ fixes $z^p$ when $p\in L$ and kills it otherwise: its coefficient is $|G|^{-1}\sum_g\chi(p)(g)$, equal to $1$ or $0$ because a nontrivial character sum is unchanged by multiplication by some value $\eta\ne1$, while $1-\eta$ is a unit: it is a factor of $\prod_{j=1}^{N-1}(1-\zeta_N^j)=N$. Thus that sum is zero. The projection statement of [lem-per-tame-invariants-arbitrary-base-change] therefore gives $\Lambda[\overline P]^G=\Lambda[\overline R]$. No henselian or sharp-chart hypothesis is being used. The $G$-invariant map from the base sends $q$ to the nonzero monomial $z^{\gamma(q)}$, so its character is trivial. Since $\gamma(q)\in P$, it belongs to $R=L\cap P$. Hence $Q\to\overline P$ factors through $R$.

source.place: X 1.8, p.147, invariant monoid calculation; VI 3.5(b); explicit monomial Reynolds calculation.

proof.text: The monoid assertions can be checked directly. $N\overline P\subset\overline R$. Write every integer unit coordinate as $Nk_i+a_i$ and every nonnegative coordinate as $Nb_i+a_i$, with $0\le a_i<N$ and $b_i\ge0$. If $p\in L\cap\overline P$, its remainder $a$ also belongs to $L$. Thus the finite set of such remainder vectors, together with $\pm N$ times the unit basis and $N$ times the nonnegative basis, generates $\overline R$. For $l\in L$, add sufficiently large nonnegative multiples of $N$ in the last $r+s$ coordinates to obtain $l+w\in\overline R$ with $w\in\overline R$; then $l=(l+w)-w$. Hence $\overline R^{\rm gp}=L$. If $l\in L$ and $kl\in\overline R$ for $k>0$, the nonnegative coordinates of $kl$ force those of $l$ to be nonnegative, so $l\in\overline R$. This proves saturation in its own group completion, and integrality is inherited from the lattice. Finally $N\mathbf Z^{t+r+s}\subset L$ gives finite index annihilated by the invertible integer $N$. The same arguments apply to $R\subset P$.

source.place: X 1.8, p.147, the Kummer invariant-monoid inclusion; direct coordinate verification.

proof.text: Take the particular smooth-functorial fan rule $\mathcal R$ of [lem-trf-functorial-fan-desingularization], not an arbitrary projective resolution. Apply it to the sharp fan of $\overline R$. Pull its ordered centers to the quotient log scheme by [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](ii). Independence of a fan chart and the overlap identifications follow from [lem-trf-strict-fan-chart-local-comparison]: strict maps identify the localized fans, and $\mathcal R$ respects those localizations and composition. Thus [lem-trf-functorial-log-blowup-etale-descent] glues this rule as the tower $F^{\log}$ used in the fourth stage. [lem-trf-monoidal-resolution-tower] supplies the finite saturated log-blowup tower with free final characteristics; its hypotheses hold because $\overline R$ is fs with lattice group completion, so all characteristic groups are torsion free. This is exactly the fan-pullback construction in VIII 3.3.14--3.3.15, not merely the existence of some resolution. The fourth-stage definition in [lem-per-gabber-absolute-equivariant-modification] prescribes this functorial quotient tower and its fs pullback.

On each successive affine chart the log-blowup formula of [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction] replaces a chart monoid $M$ by $\langle M,h-e\rangle^{\rm sat}\subset M^{\rm gp}$. That statement gives fineness and equality of group completions at each step. Starting from $\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[\overline R]$, the charts therefore have the form $\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[\overline R']$ and $\nu^{\rm gp}$ is an isomorphism. The final smooth fan gives $\overline R'/\overline R'^\times\cong\mathbf N^b$ by the definition in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. The unit group is a subgroup of the lattice and is finite free by [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free], say $\mathbf Z^a$. Lift the $b$ free sharp generators to $\overline R'$. Every element is a unique unit plus a nonnegative sum of these lifts, which identifies $\overline R'$ with $\mathbf Z^a\oplus\mathbf N^b$. This also follows from [lem-trf-toric-monoid-comparison](iii) over $\mathbf Q$; its (i)--(ii) explain the monoid centers and saturated affine charts underlying the characteristic-zero construction of the fan rule. No toric theorem over $\mathbf Q$ is applied to a scheme over $\Lambda$.

Write $T=V(z_1\cdots z_r)$ in $Y=\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[\overline P]$ and $Y_1=\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[\overline R]$. The invariant monomial $f=(z_1\cdots z_r)^N$ belongs to $\Lambda[R]$. Its inverse-image zero set in $Y$ is exactly $T$. Since $Y\to Y_1$ has orbit fibres, the image boundary $T_1=T/G$ is $V(f)$ set-theoretically. On a resolved chart the monomial $\nu(f)$ is a unit times $x_1^{d_1}\cdots x_b^{d_b}$, with $d_i\ge0$. Consequently $h_1^{-1}|T_1|$ is precisely the union of the coordinate divisors with $d_i>0$. Relabel them $1,\ldots,c$. This proves that the inverse image of the original boundary is a union of coordinate divisors, rather than presupposing it. The reduced boundary is strict normal crossings on this regular Laurent-polynomial chart. By [lem-per-regular-boundary-divisorial-chart] its divisorial log structure is generated by these $c$ coordinates together with units, so it has chart $R'=\mathbf Z^a\oplus\mathbf N^c$.

source.place: VIII 5.3.8, p.125, the invariant power defining the quotient boundary; X 1.8--1.9, pp.147--148.

proof.text:
If $g\in R$, its monomial on $Y$ involves no $y_i$ and its zero set is contained in $T$. Since it is invariant, its zero set on $Y_1$ is contained in $T_1$ (use the orbit fibres in [lem-per-very-tame-log-quotient]). Pulling back along $h_1$ gives $V(
u(g))\subset h_1^{-1}|T_1|$. In the regular chart of Step 7 a monomial has this property exactly when its exponents at $x_{c+1},\ldots,x_b$ are zero: a positive exponent would make the corresponding coordinate divisor part of its zero set, and conversely there are no other monomial zeros. Thus $
u(g)\in R'$, proving $
u(R)\subset R'$. This is the zero-locus argument that constructs the dashed arrows of diagram (1.d). Every group map in that diagram is now the group completion of the actual monoid map $Q	o R	o R'	o\overline R'$.

The chart inclusion $R'\subset\overline R'$ gives
$\Lambda[R']=\Lambda[\mathbf Z^a][x_1,\ldots,x_c]$ and
$\Lambda[\overline R']=\Lambda[R'][x_{c+1},\ldots,x_b]$.
Indeed both sides have the same monomial basis and the same multiplication. The induced scheme map is therefore affine space of dimension $b-c$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[R']$. This includes $c=0$, $c=b$, and $b=0$. The factorization proved above supplies its structure map from $\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[Q]$.

source.place: X 1.8, pp.147--148, diagram (1.d); monoid-ring basis calculation.

proof.text:
For an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset S$ put $A=\Lambda[Q]$. Its $G$-action is trivial. By [lem-per-tame-invariants-arbitrary-base-change],
$$(B\otimes_A\Lambda[\overline P])^G=B\otimes_A\Lambda[\overline R].$$
Thus taking the quotient commutes with this base change even when $A\to B$ is not flat. On $Y_1$ itself the quotient log structure $(q_*M_Y)^G$ is the canonical log structure of the chart $\overline R$: by [lem-per-very-tame-quotient-log-regular] (with Step 2 and the generic freeness of Step 11) the former is log regular with triviality locus $Y_1\setminus q(\overline T)=\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[L]$; the latter is log regular by [lem-per-log-smooth-invertible-torsion-log-regular] over $\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda$ with chart $0\to\overline R$, and is trivial exactly where all monomials of $\overline R$, hence of $L=\overline R^{\rm gp}$, are units. Both therefore equal $\mathcal O\cap j_*\mathcal O^\times$ by [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure]. The quotient log structure after base change is the strict pullback of this chart, since all chart monoid maps are unchanged by this strict base change. The map $S\to\Sigma$ is strict. Consequently its log base change is strict and the underlying scheme fibre product already has an fs log structure (the one pulled back from the toric model); no extra saturation of the underlying scheme occurs here. Strict-base-change compatibility of [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](ii) identifies the quotient resolution tower with the pullback of $F^{\log}(Y_1)$. On each resulting chart the quotient scheme is $S\times_\Sigma\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[\overline R']$ and the retained log structure has chart $R'$ by Step 7.

source.place: X 1.8, pp.146--148; VIII 3.3.10; Reynolds extension for the possibly non-flat strict base change.

proof.text:
The enlarged pair $(Y,\overline T)$, with $\overline T=V(z_1\cdots z_ry_1\cdots y_s)$, is log regular: locally its stratum ring is a localization of $\Lambda[\mathbf Z^t]$ and its nonunit parameters are a subset of the $z_i,y_j$. The model action is generically free: by the inert comparison below, any element acting trivially on the model also fixes the source over its torus, where the original action is free. Its action is very tame, since all parameters are eigenvectors and inertia fixes the unit coordinates and the residual log strata. By [lem-per-very-tame-log-quotient], its map to $(Y_1,\overline T_1)$ is a Kummer etale $G$-cover. By [lem-per-kummer-g-cover-fs-base-change] the fs pullback along the resolved quotient tower is again a $G$-cover with that resolved scheme as its quotient. This justifies quotient identification after the fs pullback, a different operation from Step 10's strict base change.

For the equivariant strict etale comparison supplied in Step 1, restrict to the inert open of [lem-per-inert-etale-quotient-comparison], which contains the distinguished point because its inertia was the whole chosen group. The enlarged base-changed pair is log regular by [lem-per-log-smooth-invertible-torsion-log-regular], since its chart is $Q\to\overline P$ with the same invertible torsion as $Q\to P$ and the smooth comparison of Step 1. Both enlarged actions are very tame. The quotient-comparison lemma therefore makes the quotient comparison etale and strict for the enlarged quotient log structures. The same comparison preserves the original boundary and its inverse image, so its restriction to the retained divisorial log structures is strict as well. Therefore the quotient of the modified $(X',Z')$ is a strict etale neighborhood of the model in Step 10.

All chart refinements respect strict base change by [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup]. On two strict inert comparison neighborhoods the quotient comparisons in [lem-per-inert-etale-quotient-comparison] identify the ordered local quotient towers, and [lem-trf-functorial-log-blowup-etale-descent] identifies their descended tower including its centers. The fourth-stage clause of [lem-per-gabber-absolute-equivariant-modification] gives independence of the enlarged boundary and compatibility with strict inertia-preserving morphisms. It follows that the locally computed towers are the stipulated global fourth stage, with boundary exactly $b^{-1}Z$. This uses the fourth-stage functoriality as stated; no relative log smoothness of the smaller unresolved boundary is assumed.
